title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within a generate–validate–repair adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.74468085%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration language and formal estimand, disclose a protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature), and document that the preregistered benign-control was not executed; all principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction:
High-level operator intents are increasingly translated into device CLI by large language models (LLMs) to accelerate NetOps workflows. However, generative drafts can violate sequencing constraints, CLI syntax, or safety invariants; adversarially mutated intents can amplify these risks. Deterministic validators (deployment gates) and template-based sanitization are common engineering defenses, but their end-to-end efficacy against adversarial intents in LLM-driven pipelines remains underexplored under preregistered confirmatory conditions. We address a narrowly scoped, operational research question that admits preregistered inference: How effective are deterministic verifier-gating and template-based input sanitization (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (cand-2026-03) that isolates post-generation guarded-pipeline effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a concise, artifact-grounded description of per-condition pipeline semantics and execution accounting; (3) confirmatory quantitative results (paired absolute difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI ≈ [0.01418,0.07801]) together with diagnostic linkage of discordant cases to permitted repairs; and (4) a clear reconciliation that validator-acceptance improvements do not, by themselves, equal reductions in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification and NetOps gating are rooted in formal, packet/state-based validators that report property-level violations rather than token-level mismatches; classic examples and modern successors demonstrate rapid, semantics-focused checks appropriate for deployment gating [1],[2]. Recent LLM-for-NetOps studies show that model-only generation often yields ordering and precondition violations and that integrating external verification and constrained repair tends to reduce observable errors on narrow tasks [3],[4],[5]. Security analyses of LLM-integrated systems document prompt-injection and indirect attacks that motivate input sanitization and gating defenses [6]. Prior benchmark work highlights heterogeneous evaluation practices and argues for validator-centered deployability metrics rather than purely lexical measures [3],[7]. Our study situates itself among these lines by preregistering a validator-acceptance estimand, using shared_initial_candidate semantics to ensure paired comparability, and providing artifact-backed traceability for interpretive diagnostics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent the binary outcome equals 1 if deterministic_netops_validator_v5 would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729).

Design, scope, and adversary model. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents (paired episodes across Baseline and Guarded). The synthetic intent templates exercise admin/MTU/VLAN changes and ordered sequencing constraints (e.g., shutdown–change–restore). The adversary applied deterministic mutation heuristics to these templates. Scope is explicitly synthetic and limited to the supplied CLI grammar encoded in the deterministic validator; no production network data were used.

Model, validator, and orchestration. Declared generator: gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration used a generate–validate–repair adapter implementing shared_initial_candidate semantics: one shared LLM draft per intent pair, baseline evaluation of that draft, and guarded processing that applied template-based sanitization and, if permitted by policy, at-most-one automated repair LLM call prior to final validation. Provider-call accounting and stage counts (shared_initial_generation vs repair) were archived in the execution manifest.

Missingness, exclusions, and preregistered but unexecuted items. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. The run recorded completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs included in primary analysis = 141. Importantly, the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the associated false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; because those items are absent, no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported and claims requiring that control are explicitly limited in Results and Discussion. A protocol deviation is disclosed: the archived execution recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature in the model configuration (temperature = null); to maintain paired comparability the run used shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call accounting confirms the single-shared-generation-per-pair pattern.
sections.results:
Execution and counts. Planned episodes = 300; completed_episodes = 282; failed_episodes = 18. After applying the preregistered exclusion rule (exclude a paired unit only when both paired runs failed), complete_pairs_included = 141. Provider-call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed = 147, failed = 9; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6.

Condition-level outcomes and paired inference. Analysis inputs (complete_pairs = 141) produced baseline_success_count = 135 (baseline success rate = 0.9574468085106383) and guarded_success_count = 141 (guarded success rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table entries are n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test yields p = 0.03125. The paired absolute estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165; bootstrap percentile 95% CI from 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numeric values and test parameters are archived in the analysis artifacts.

Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant n10 pairs are traceable to the guarded pipeline and to the repair stage: stage_counts.repair = 6, and per-episode validator traces indicate repair_applied = true for episodes that converted a draft the baseline validator rejected into a final candidate the validator accepted. In these cases acceptance followed either sanitizer normalization/slot-filling or the single permitted automated repair; the shared_initial_candidate for each pair is identical between baseline and guarded artifacts, consistent with the registered shared_initial_candidate semantics. These diagnostics show that the guarded pipeline increased validator acceptance by recovering reparable drafts rather than by rejecting benign drafts.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs were technical failures. As a conservative sensitivity check (not the preregistered primary analysis), treating those excluded pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; this changes margins but not the direction of the observed paired difference under this conservative assumption.

Unexecuted preregistered analyses. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking statistics are available. This omission reduces the ability to quantify guarded-pipeline false-positive blocking and is explicitly accounted for in the interpretation below.
sections.discussion:
Interpretive reconciliation. The preregistration's natural-language H1 framed verifier-gating as a defense reducing attacker success. The formal estimand measured validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). The observed guarded→higher acceptance (≈4.255 percentage points) arises because sanitizer and bounded repair converted some initially rejected drafts into validator-accepted candidates. Thus, the formal-estimand improvement does not directly demonstrate reduced attacker success under attacker-centric definitions; it demonstrates increased validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline and highlights the need for an independent semantic-safety oracle when attacker success is the target quantity.

Operational implications and co-design. Within the synthetic setting, guarded pipelines that include template sanitization and bounded automatic repair can reduce operator rework by producing validator-accepted candidates. However, this benefit depends critically on: (a) validator expressiveness (what safety properties are encoded), (b) repair scope constraints (bounded repairs vs unconstrained edits), and (c) the provenance of repaired edits (sanitizer vs LLM repair). Repairs that preserve intent are beneficial; repairs that mask adversarial manipulations risk increasing deployment hazard. Thus deployment requires co-design of gating policies, repair bounds, and validator coverage.

Threats to validity and generalization. Internal validity: technical failures (18/300) reduced effective sample size; preregistered exclusions were applied. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar and sequencing invariants but does not capture all protocol-level behaviors; acceptance is a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: a single generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and synthetic intent bank limit generalization across vendors, CLI dialects, and production environments. Conclusion validity: a ceiling effect (guarded = 100%) and small discordant count (n10 = 6) mean the practical significance should be evaluated in operational context, not inferred solely from statistical detectability.

Practical recommendations. (1) Execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking before operational deployment. (2) When the policy objective concerns attacker success, preregister an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle (e.g., reachability tests). (3) Diversify generators and validators across vendors and CLI dialects before claiming broader generality. (4) For deterministic reproduction, explicitly set provider sampling (e.g., temperature = 0) rather than relying on provider defaults; the archived run recorded temperature = null and this is disclosed as a protocol deviation.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI ≈ [0.01418,0.07801]). Diagnostics link the six discordant pairs to permitted repair activity that enabled acceptance. Crucially, validator-acceptance improvements do not equate to measured reductions in attacker success without an independent semantic-safety oracle. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent oracle, diversify models/validators, and fix sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers reported here are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (declared in the archived model configuration), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family implemented a generate–validate–repair workflow with shared_initial_candidate semantics. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered and archived prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null); this is disclosed because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism. Provider-call accounting and execution manifest evidence were archived per the execution manifest; full execution and analysis artifacts are available in the archived execution bundle. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
